key_insight: SARA treats rollout collection as a sequential stop/continue decision, using early evidence to stop wasted work on saturated prompts and redirect budget to prompts that still have learning signal.
engineering_relevance: For RLVR training, this can cut rollout cost substantially while preserving or improving the quality of policy-gradient updates, making training more compute-efficient on limited hardware.
method: Maintain a Beta posterior for each prompt’s success rate.
Use a closed-form estimate of whether a group will be effective, then apply a two-threshold SPRT-style rule to commit, abandon, or continue.
Reallocate saved rollout budget to new prompts without extra prediction rollouts.
evidence_signal: On mathematical reasoning and planning tasks with 1.5B/3B models on a single GPU, SARA matched DPS while using 22% fewer rollouts than dynamic sampling, and SARA+DPS achieved the best accuracy at 67% fewer rollouts.
watch_item: The sequential decision rule depends on posterior calibration and threshold tuning, so performance may be sensitive when reward noise or prompt difficulty shifts sharply during training.
paper_title: Early Verdicts, Better Budgets: Sequential Adaptive Rollout Allocation for Compute-Efficient RLVR
